# Rollout Plan: Migrating 40,000 Users to New Billing System

## Overview
This plan migrates 40,000 existing users from the legacy billing system to the new billing system in three phases, with both systems running in parallel (dual-write/dual-run) throughout the migration window. The old system remains fully operational until well after the final user batch has been migrated and validated.

---

## Phase 1: Pilot (5% of users — 2,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed end-to-end integration testing in staging, including successful test transactions for all supported payment methods and currencies; rollback procedure has been dry-run and verified; on-call runbook is published.

**Scope:** Internal accounts, employee accounts, and opted-in low-risk external customers (e.g., customers on monthly plans with no active disputes).

**Activities:**
- Enable dual-write so both systems record transactions.
- Migrate account and billing history for the pilot cohort.
- Compare invoices, charges, and balances line-by-line between old and new systems daily.
- Collect support ticket volume and reconciliation discrepancies.

**Exit criterion:** 7 consecutive days with reconciliation match rate ≥ 99.9% and no unresolved P1/P2 incidents.

---

## Phase 2: Expansion (30% of users — 12,000 users, cumulative 35%)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 exit criteria met; engineering has closed all P1/P2 defects found in Phase 1; customer support team has been trained on new-system troubleshooting.

**Scope:** Broader mix of customer segments, including different plan types, payment methods, and geographies, migrated in sub-waves of ~2,000–3,000 users every 3–5 days to allow monitoring between waves.

**Activities:**
- Continue dual-write and daily reconciliation.
- Introduce automated reconciliation alerting (not just manual review).
- Begin monitoring customer-facing metrics: failed payment rate, support ticket rate, billing-related churn.
- Load test new system at higher throughput.

**Exit criterion:** 14 consecutive days with reconciliation match rate ≥ 99.9%, failed-payment rate within 0.1 percentage points of legacy system baseline, and support ticket volume attributable to billing not elevated more than 10% over baseline.

---

## Phase 3: Full Migration (65% of users — 26,000 users, cumulative 100%)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 exit criteria met; capacity testing confirms new system can handle 100% of production load with headroom; finance/accounting has signed off on ledger reconciliation accuracy; legal/compliance sign-off obtained for full cutover (e.g., tax handling, invoicing regulations).

**Scope:** All remaining users, migrated in sub-waves (e.g., 5 waves of ~5,200 users) over 2–3 weeks, with a freeze on new migrations if any halt threshold is triggered.

**Activities:**
- Continue dual-write through the final batch and for a defined post-migration observation window.
- Full parity monitoring dashboards live for finance and support teams.
- Prepare (but do not execute) old-system read-only/retirement plan — this is explicitly a **separate, later phase** (see Note below).

**Exit criterion:** 100% of users migrated, 30 consecutive days of reconciliation match rate ≥ 99.9%, zero unresolved billing-critical defects, and finance sign-off on full-period ledger closing using new system data.

> **Note on decommissioning:** Retiring, disabling, or decommissioning the old billing system is intentionally excluded from Phase 3 and treated as a distinct **Phase 4 (Legacy Decommission)**, which begins only after a minimum 30–60 day parallel-run observation period following 100% migration, with its own separate entry criteria (e.g., a full billing cycle and audit closed successfully on the new system alone).

---

## Risks

RISK: Data corruption or mismatched balances during migration of a user's billing history | Run automated daily reconciliation jobs comparing old vs. new ledgers per user, with automatic quarantine of mismatched accounts before they proceed to next phase | Data Migration Lead
RISK: Payment processor integration failures causing duplicate or failed charges | Implement idempotency keys on all payment calls and run shadow transactions in the new system before enabling live charging per cohort | Payments Engineering Lead
RISK: Customer-facing outage or billing errors eroding trust and increasing churn | Maintain dual-write with instant rollback capability per user cohort and staff support team with escalation path during each wave | Customer Support Manager
RISK: New system cannot handle full production load at 100% migration | Conduct load/capacity testing at 2x expected peak volume before Phase 3 entry and maintain autoscaling headroom | Site Reliability Engineering Lead
RISK: Regulatory/tax compliance gaps in new system for certain jurisdictions | Legal and compliance review of tax/invoicing rules per region prior to migrating users in that region, with phased regional rollout | Compliance Officer

---

## Halt Metric

If at any point the **reconciliation mismatch rate exceeds 0.5%** of transactions (i.e., match rate falls below 99.5%) over any rolling 24-hour period, the rollout is immediately halted, no further users are migrated to the next wave/phase, and the incident response process is triggered until root cause is resolved and match rate is restored to ≥ 99.9% for 48 consecutive hours.

Additional halt triggers:
- Failed-payment rate increases by more than 0.2 percentage points versus the legacy-system baseline for any 24-hour period.
- Billing-related support ticket volume increases more than 25% over the pre-migration baseline in any 24-hour period.

PHASES: 3
